headline: CHINA EXTENDS RARE EARTH EXPORT PAUSE TO JANUARY 2027 — NOVEMBER 10 BINARY CLEARED FOR USAR AND MP MATERIALS
snippet: China's Ministry of Commerce formally extended its suspension of the expanded October 2025 rare earth, battery-material and superhard-material export controls to January 10, 2027 — removing the November 10 cliff the previous queue flagged as a binary event for USA Rare Earth (NYSE: USAR) and other Western rare earth equities. The paused measures include the extraterritorial '0.1% rule' on foreign goods containing Chinese rare earth content and licensing for holmium, erbium, thulium, europium and ytterbium; the original April 2025 controls on seven medium and heavy rare earths remain in force and were not part of the suspension. For retail investors in the rare earth sector, the extension closes the near-term downside scenario but does not remove the structural supply-chain risk that makes Western rare earth developers strategically relevant: the January 10, 2027 date aligns closely with the Pentagon's DFARS cutoff for Chinese-sourced magnets in defence procurement, meaning the next binary is already visible on the calendar.

headline: GOLD TOUCHES $4,112 MONDAY MORNING — UP 1% ON BARRICK TAILWIND, $4,150 TARGET BEFORE WEDNESDAY CPI
snippet: Spot gold climbed to $4,112 per ounce Monday morning — up approximately 1% on the day and roughly $50 above Friday's close — extending the momentum from Barrick's strong Q3 beat as markets positioned ahead of Wednesday's U.S. CPI release. Reuters logged gold at $4,123 by 04:28 GMT, while Kitco's morning snapshot put it at $4,096 at 5:41 a.m. ET; analysts identify $4,150 as the next meaningful resistance and $4,000 as the floor to defend if CPI surprises to the upside and the dollar firms. Silver tracked higher alongside gold, with futures near $53-54, pushing the gold-silver ratio toward 78x and reinforcing the structural argument that silver remains undervalued relative to gold at current prices. For TSX-V junior gold investors, Monday's move confirms that Barrick's earnings result has successfully bridged the market to the next macro catalyst without a post-earnings selloff.

headline: PURSUIT MINERALS + ECOPRO: $40M SOUTH KOREAN BATTERY DEAL — 20% STAKE AND 100% OFFTAKE AT RIO GRANDE SUR
snippet: Pursuit Minerals (ASX: PUR) announced today a non-binding MoU with South Korea's EcoPro Innovation — the upstream arm of leading battery cathode maker EcoPro — under which EcoPro would invest US$20 million for a 20% stake in the Argentine subsidiary holding the Rio Grande Sur lithium project in Salta Province, plus up to US$20 million in advance funding, in exchange for 100% offtake of the project's initial 5,000-tonne-per-year LCE production. Stage 1 development at Rio Grande Sur requires approximately US$120 million in debt financing against a total funding requirement of US$156 million, and EcoPro's equity and advance commitment materially de-risks that financing stack. The deal follows Rio Tinto's $1.4 billion commitment to its own Argentine lithium operations and Eramet's parallel Centenario stake-sale process — signalling that South Korean battery manufacturers are actively competing with Chinese processors to lock in upstream lithium supply from the Argentine brine triangle while spot prices remain below incentive levels.

headline: ERAMET IN TALKS TO SELL CENTENARIO LITHIUM AND WEDA BAY NICKEL STAKES — ARIZARO CONCESSIONS SOLD FOR $71M
snippet: French diversified miner Eramet confirmed today it has received expressions of interest from multiple potential partners for minority stakes in its Centenario lithium operation in Argentina — currently producing 24,000 t/y LCE with a long-term expansion potential of 150,000 t/y — and said investors have signalled interest in a 'significant portion' of its minority stake in the Weda Bay nickel operation in Indonesia. Separately, Eramet confirmed a binding agreement to sell undeveloped Arizaro salt flat lithium concessions in Argentina for US$71 million, expected to close before year-end. The simultaneous stake-sale processes across both lithium and nickel assets reflect the broader trend of European mining majors seeking strategic co-investors to fund critical mineral expansions at a moment when downstream battery manufacturers — particularly South Korean firms — are aggressively building upstream equity positions to secure supply ahead of the next EV demand wave.

headline: UR-ENERGY Q3 DUE AFTER THE BELL — SHIRLEY BASIN RESTART LEAVES SPARE CAPACITY, WYOMING EXPANSION IN PLAY
snippet: Ur-Energy (NYSE: URG / TSX: URE) releases its Q3 2026 financial and operating results after the close today, with a management call and webcast scheduled for November 10 at 11 a.m. ET. Ahead of the release, The Northern Miner's interview with the company reveals that the restart of its Shirley Basin uranium mine in Wyoming has left spare processing capacity that management is now looking to fill through additional drilling, acquisitions, or third-party processing arrangements — a growth playbook that mirrors the capacity-driven M&A logic seen at other ISR uranium producers. Analyst consensus for Q3 sits at ($0.04) per share on roughly $14.4 million in revenue, with Q2 2026 showing a low cash cost of $40.20/lb on 140,873 lb produced. For uranium sector investors, Ur-Energy's Q3 is the second in a string of late-week uranium producer earnings — Uranium Energy Corp already reported a miss on higher spending — and tonight's result will add to the market's picture of which ISR producers are capturing the benefit of long-term contracts signed above current spot prices.

headline: URANIUM ENERGY Q3 MISS — HIGHER SPENDING CLIPS EARNINGS AS SECTOR DIGESTS DUAL PRODUCER EARNINGS WEEK
snippet: Uranium Energy Corp (NYSE: UEC) reported Q3 fiscal 2026 results that missed analyst earnings estimates, with higher exploration and development spending absorbing the revenue contribution from contracted uranium deliveries. The miss follows a period where UEC has been investing aggressively in its Texas ISR hub and Wyoming asset base, prioritising production capacity ahead of a spot price environment where long-term contract pricing remains more attractive than current spot. Uranium equities as a whole are down more than 50% since the beginning of 2026 despite the long-term uranium price rising 12% year-to-date — a disconnect that reflects equity market skepticism about near-term production timelines and operating cost execution at projects that looked more straightforward when uranium was rallying in 2024-2025.

headline: SCHIFF: POLITICAL SHIFT WILL SEND INFLATION SOARING — 'THIS IS JUST A SIGN OF THINGS TO COME' FOR GOLD
snippet: Peter Schiff, the veteran gold bull and economist, argued in a widely-circulated post-midterm commentary that the Democrats' midterm sweep creates the fiscal conditions for a sustained inflationary spiral that will drive gold materially higher — framing gold mining stocks' emergence as 'a rare bright spot' during the equity selloff as an early signal of the rotation he has long anticipated. Schiff's analysis echoes the structural case made by the VanEck Gold Miners ETF's outperformance relative to the broader market in the wake of the midterm results, though it goes further in predicting that expanding government spending commitments from the new congressional alignment will overwhelm the Warsh Fed's ability to hold the line on inflation. For retail junior mining investors skeptical of newsletter-style gold hype, Schiff's track record is mixed — but the gold miners-as-inflation-hedge thesis is the same one that drove the last decade's major bull runs in TSX-V gold producers.

headline: GOLD-SILVER RATIO EXPANDS TO 78.5x — SIXTH STRAIGHT SILVER SUPPLY DEFICIT MEANS THE GAP SHOULD NARROW
snippet: A GoldSeek analysis puts the gold-silver ratio at approximately 78.5x — with gold near $4,080 and silver below its structural implied value at current deficit conditions — and argues that silver's sustained outflow from ETP holdings (down roughly 60 million ounces year-to-date) has been masking a physical market that has run a supply deficit for five consecutive years and is on track for a sixth. The piece notes that mean reversion in the ratio toward the historical range of 60-70x would imply silver prices in the $58-68 range at current gold levels — a 15-30% upside that is not being priced in despite persistent industrial demand from solar and electronics. For ASX and TSX-V silver developers, the GoldSeek analysis provides the same fundamental support case that has animated the sector all year: a physical market in structural deficit at a price that is not yet incentivising new supply, while the silver-gold ratio gap invites capital rotation from gold ETF holders seeking relative value within the precious metals complex.

headline: POLAND NBP CHIEF EYES MORE GOLD AFTER 700-TONNE TARGET — CENTRAL BANK BUYING CYCLE NOT OVER
snippet: Poland's National Bank chief signalled that the central bank remains open to buying gold beyond its recently achieved 700-tonne target — a statement that extends one of the most aggressive central bank gold accumulation programmes in recent years and reinforces the structural demand thesis that has underpinned gold's rally to $4,000+. Poland's buying programme has been driven by an explicit policy of reducing exposure to USD-denominated reserve assets and diversifying into physical gold held domestically — a strategy that multiple Central and Eastern European central banks have pursued since Russia's 2022 invasion demonstrated the geopolitical risk of foreign-held currency reserves. For gold market investors, the NBP statement is incremental evidence that the central bank demand impulse that helped drive gold from $2,000 to $4,000+ is not exhausted even at current price levels.

headline: 134 NEW LITHIUM MINES NEEDED BY 2050 AS GLOBAL DEMAND TARGETS 7 MILLION TONNES LCE — SMM MAPS THE SUPPLY GAP
snippet: Shanghai Metals Market's long-range lithium demand modelling projects global consumption rising from 2.11 million tonnes LCE in 2026 to approximately 7 million tonnes LCE by 2050 — a 4.9 million tonne increase driven overwhelmingly by electric vehicles, which the model assigns 76% of the growth. Meeting that demand would require an estimated 134 new lithium mines at average project scale, far exceeding the pipeline currently under development or in construction globally. The analysis is a timely counter-narrative to the near-term bearishness visible in spot lithium carbonate prices and the Citi 40% forecast cut: the structural demand build that justifies long-lead-time project development is not dependent on 2026 spot prices — it is dependent on EV adoption trajectories that have not changed despite the near-term lithium oversupply. For junior lithium developers on the TSX-V and ASX building projects with 2029-2032 first-production targets, the 134-mine figure frames the investment case in its correct multi-decade context.
